title: AlphaPilot Task State Contract
description: Machine-readable cross-language contract for task state lifecycle, legacy status mapping, and validation rules. This is the single source of truth for Python Worker, Node API, and TypeScript Extension.

meta.authority: Python Worker (task_state_contract.py) is the authoritative source. Node and Extension consume and validate; they do not originate state changes.
meta.conflict_rule: task_state is authoritative. If task_state and legacy status conflict, the result is invalid — no silent resolution.

task_states.description: Task lifecycle states. Five legal values, no others permitted.

semantic_notes.WAITING_AUTHORIZATION: Task is blocked pending user authorization via Extension. It is NOT a failure, NOT a completion, and must not be forwarded as done/error/pending. The Extension gate may allow partial FileOps only when matching authorization_requests exist in the payload.

step_states.description: Per-step execution states within a task. Six legal values.

compatibility.description: For each task_state, which step_states are legal.

transitions.description: Legal task_state → task_state transitions. from=null means initial creation. Any transition not listed in 'legal' is illegal. The 'illegal' list below is Python's explicit enumeration for test assertions; it is illustrative, not exhaustive.

legacy_status_mapping.description: Bidirectional mapping between task_state and legacy 'status' field (used by older Workers and protocol v3).

completed.condition: Only accepted when task_state is COMPLETED. Treated as a warning-level compatibility alias, not a separate legal value.
completed.example: { task_state: 'COMPLETED', status: 'completed' } → valid (with warning), resolved status = 'done'

validation_rules.description: Rules applied by resolveStatus() (Node) / resolveTaskStatus() (TS) / validate_result_contract() (Python). All three layers must produce identical validity judgments for the same input.

scenarios.rationale: Cannot determine task outcome. Must not default to done or error.

scenarios.input: task_state present and in legal set, status missing
scenarios.expected: valid=true, status=forward_mapping[task_state] (with warning about missing status)

scenarios.input: task_state missing, status present and in reverse mapping
scenarios.expected: valid=true, status=status_value (with warning about missing task_state)
scenarios.rationale: Backward compatibility for old Workers that only emit status.

scenarios.input: task_state missing, status present but NOT in reverse mapping (unknown value)
scenarios.rationale: Cannot trust unknown status values. Must not map unknown → done.

scenarios.input: task_state present but NOT in legal set (unknown value)
scenarios.rationale: Unknown task_state is a hard contract violation.

scenarios.input: both present, task_state → status matches forward mapping
scenarios.rationale: Clean case; no violations or warnings.

scenarios.input: both present, task_state → status conflicts with forward mapping (field conflict)
scenarios.rationale: task_state is authoritative; conflicting status is a contract violation. Must not silently pick one.

scenarios.expected: valid=true, status='done' (with warning about compatibility alias)
scenarios.rationale: Legacy alias 'completed' accepted only when task_state is COMPLETED. Other combinations with 'completed' are S7 conflicts.

audit_events.description: Contract-level audit events recorded during task execution.

error_codes.description: Protocol-level error codes emitted by Worker and validated by Node.

notes.CONTRACT_VIOLATION: Raised when an illegal state transition is attempted (replaces assert transition_is_legal). Must not be silently downgraded to MODEL_CALL_ERROR or UNKNOWN_ERROR.

migration.description: Versioning and migration strategy for this contract.

changes: Initial machine-readable contract extracted from Python task_state_contract.py v0.2 (G1.1), Node taskStateContract.js (G3.1), and TypeScript taskModel.ts (G3.1).
All five task states, their terminal classification, and legal/illegal transitions defined.
All six step states and their compatibility matrix with task states defined.
Bidirectional legacy status mapping with compatibility alias 'completed'.
Eight validation scenarios (S1–S8) as the cross-language truth table.
Ten audit events, forbidden pairs, and idempotency key format.

migration.note: All three known divergences resolved. 59/59 shared vectors pass across Python, Node.js, and TypeScript.

changes.python: Added .trim() processing, unknown status rejection, 'completed' alias in validate_result_contract(). Added VALID_LEGACY_STATUS_VALUES constant.
changes.node: Added .trim() processing for task_state and status in resolveStatus().
changes.typescript: Rewrote resolveTaskStatus(): now rejects unknown status-only values (S4), detects field conflicts (S7), handles 'completed' alias (S3), trims whitespace (S8). Added VALID_STATUS_VALUES constant.

usage.description: How each layer should consume this Schema.

python.action: Load constants and mappings from this JSON via json.load(). Remove hand-written TASK_STATES_ALL, TASK_STATE_TO_LEGACY_STATUS, LEGAL_TRANSITIONS, etc. Keep validate_result_contract() logic; it reads the loaded data.
python.authority: Python Worker remains the authority for state transitions. Schema is a reference, not a runtime enforcement replacement.

node.action: Load via require('./contract-schema.json'). Replace hand-written TASK_STATE_VALUES, TASK_STATE_TO_STATUS, TERMINAL_TASK_STATES. Keep resolveStatus() logic; it reads the loaded data.
node.authority: Node API validates and forwards. It does not originate state changes.

typescript.action: Import via import schema from '../../contract-schema.json' (with resolveJsonModule). Replace hand-written TASK_STATE_VALUES, TASK_STATE_TO_STATUS. Fix resolveTaskStatus() to match S4 and S7 validation rules. Keep isTaskSuccess/Error/Pending and validateTaskResult().
typescript.authority: Extension validates before consuming side effects (FileOps, UI). It does not originate state changes.

test_vectors.description: Placeholder for G3.2-2: a separate JSON array of test vectors consumed by Python, Node, and TypeScript test suites to verify identical validation behavior.
test_vectors.note: Will be defined in contract-test-vectors.json (G3.2-2). Each vector: { input: {task_state?, status?}, expected: {valid, status?, violations?, warnings?} }.
